LESSON: MONEY (KENYAN CURRENCY)- COINS.

Grade: SNE  /  physical-impairment / PP2
Subject: General
Strand: Measurement
Topic 3.5: Money (Kenyan currency)- coins.
Suggested lessons in curriculum: 8

SECTION 1: INTRODUCTION

This lesson covers Money (Kenyan currency)- coins., part of Measurement in SNE  /  physical-impairment / PP2 General.

Key inquiry question: What can you see on the coin?

You will study the official KICD learning outcomes, classroom activities, values, and competencies for this topic. Use Kenyan examples from your county, school, and community throughout.

SECTION 2: LEARNING OUTCOMES

By the end of this topic, you should be able to:

Refer to the KICD curriculum reference at the end of this lesson for the full list of outcomes.

SECTION 3: KEY CONCEPTS AND EXPLANATION

A. Suggested learning experiences (from KICD)

1. Look at and talk about different coins in Kenyan currency; Ksh.1, Ksh.5, Ksh.10 and Ksh.20 in purposive pairs/groups. Learners with speech difficulties could use Alternative and Augmentative modes of Communication (AAC) to sare their views.

2. Identify in purposive pairs/groups Kenyan coins; Ksh.1, Ksh.5, Ksh.10, Ksh.20. Learners with manipulation difficulties could use alternative functional parts of the body or appropriate assistive technology such as universal cuffs to identify the Kenyan coins.

3. Count Ksh.1 coin up to 20 in purposive pairs/groups.

4. Work with peers to count Ksh.1 coin up to 20.

SECTION 4: LEARNING ACTIVITIES

A. At school

1. Look at and talk about different coins in Kenyan currency; Ksh.1, Ksh.5, Ksh.10 and Ksh.20 in purposive pairs/groups. Learners with speech difficulties could use Alternative and Augmentative modes of Communication (AAC) to sare their views.
2. Identify in purposive pairs/groups Kenyan coins; Ksh.1, Ksh.5, Ksh.10, Ksh.20. Learners with manipulation difficulties could use alternative functional parts of the body or appropriate assistive technology such as universal cuffs to identify the Kenyan coins.
3. Count Ksh.1 coin up to 20 in purposive pairs/groups.
4. Work with peers to count Ksh.1 coin up to 20.

B. At home with your parent or guardian

1. Read this lesson on Money (Kenyan currency)- coins. together.
2. Discuss the key inquiry question and give examples from your area.
3. Write five sentences summarising what you learned.
4. Prepare for the revision quiz at the end of this topic.

SECTION 5: CORE COMPETENCIES, VALUES, AND PCIs

Core Competencies to be developed:
Citizenship: learners identify different Kenyan currency coins used in the market (Ksh.1, Ksh.5, Ksh.10, Ksh.20).

Values:
Responsibility: learners take turns counting Kenyan currency coins Ksh.1 up to 20.

Pertinent and Contemporary Issues:
(PCIs):

Financial literacy: learners identify Kenyan currency coins for distinguishing one coin from the other.

Link to Other Activity Areas:

The learner is able to relate new vocabulary related to different coins in Kenyan currency (Ksh.1, Ksh.5, Ksh.10, Ksh.20) to

their use in reading skill in Language Activities.
